text.tspan: Mean and Standard Deviation of Spore Shape

tspan.tspan: Figure 3. Most variation in spore shape is explained by one axis
of variation (elongate to globose) and this axis is significantly
correlated with spore volume. (A) Variation in
Amanita
spore
shape along the axes of the top 3 principal components. Principal
component 1 (PC1) is analogous to the “elongate-globose”
spectrum qualitatively described by taxonomists. Principal
component 2 (PC2) represents the placement of the hilar
appendix. Principal component 3 (PC3) represents the
prominence of the hilar appendix. (B)
Variance explained by first
5 principal components
. Principal component 1 explains the vast
majority of variation in spore shape. (C) Spore volume and PC1
are significantly correlated (r = 0.31, r² = 0.10, p < 0.001). Each
point represents a single species. Visually exceptional data points
on the extremities are labeled with species names for descriptive
purposes only. Elongate spores appear constrained to be
smaller, large spores appear constrained to be more globose,
and small spores appear to be both elongate and globose.
